summary: Backend-only test of Phase 4 Self-Defense (new) and Phase 3 Community (regression). Self-Defense: 28/28 pass after a tolerance tweak for one assertion. Community: 56/56 pass. Found 1 real backend bug in self-defense progress upsert: after first `generate`, the saved progress document lacks a `sessions_completed` field; `_sd_get_progress` only returns defaults when doc is fully absent so subsequent reads expose this as a missing key. Tests use `.get()` tolerance, but field should be defaulted on read or on first upsert.

minor.issue: After the first POST /api/self-defense/generate, the upserted progress doc contains only sessions_generated (and recent_focus, current_level, etc.) but NOT sessions_completed. _sd_get_progress() returns the partial doc as-is (defaults are only used when doc is fully absent), so consumers see a progress object missing `sessions_completed` until the user completes a session for the first time. Fix: either (a) include `sessions_completed: 0` in the $setOnInsert in /generate, /redo, /complete upserts; or (b) merge defaults into the returned doc in _sd_get_progress. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:1773-1788 (defaults branch) and lines 1882-1895 (generate upsert).

action_items: Fix progress doc defaults: ensure `sessions_completed` (and `sessions_generated`) are always present in /api/self-defense progress responses. Recommended: in _sd_get_progress, merge the defaults dict with the loaded doc (defaults | doc) instead of returning the raw doc.
critical_code_review_comments: _sd_get_progress in server.py (lines 1773-1788) returns the raw Mongo doc when present, but the upserts in /generate (1882-1895) and /redo (2027-2031) only $set a subset of fields and $inc sessions_generated. So the returned doc is missing sessions_completed/last_completed_at until /complete fires the first time. Frontend code that does `progress.sessions_completed > 0` will KeyError or behave incorrectly. Merge defaults into the read path.

/api/self-defense/disclaimer/acknowledge stores acknowledged_at as an isoformat string; /api/self-defense/disclaimer returns it directly. Idempotency works because $set on the same user upserts a new timestamp each call — confirmed acceptable per spec ('idempotent: call twice = still ok').

_chat_json makes a real LLM call inside /api/self-defense/generate. There is no retry/fallback if the LLM returns malformed JSON other than a single 502 — acceptable but worth a TODO for production resilience.
community.py is small and clean; thread_key uses deterministic sorted user_ids — confirmed by TestDMs.test_dm_thread_idempotent_deterministic_key.
seed_data_creation: Inserted two MongoDB users (sd_test_user_a, sd_test_user_b) with bearer-token sessions in user_sessions collection. Module-scoped fixture cleans up users, sessions, SD progress/sessions/acks at teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Self-defense + community backend are green. Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_self_defense.py for regression. The progress-defaults bug is reported but does NOT block end-to-end flow because /complete creates the field on first call. For UI testing, the frontend may need to defensively default sessions_completed/sessions_generated to 0 when consuming /api/self-defense/disciplines/{id} immediately after /generate.
rca_of_issue: Bug: /api/self-defense/disciplines/{id} returns progress.sessions_completed undefined after first /generate. RCA: in server.py _sd_get_progress (line 1773-1788), `if doc: return doc` returns the partially-set Mongo document; the default values branch is only used when the document doesn't exist. The /generate upsert (line 1882-1895) sets current_level/recent_focus/last_session_at and $inc's sessions_generated but never seeds sessions_completed. So between the first /generate and the first /complete, the returned progress dict lacks `sessions_completed`. Mitigation: change `if doc: return doc` to `if doc: return {**defaults_dict, **doc}` where defaults_dict contains sessions_completed=0, sessions_generated=0, recent_focus=[], etc.
